lessons.title: Read the concession and the conclusion
lessons.description: Read the notice and quoted editorial without assuming permanent approval.
lessons.canDo: Separate a concession from the final recommendation.

lessons.title: Keep the scope of a public proposal
lessons.description: Track the stated proposal, its restriction and the information needed to decide.
lessons.canDo: Preserve scope and practical conditions when summarising an argument.

lessons.title: A smaller proposal is still a proposal
lessons.description: Compare a prior proposal with a later response while keeping evidence limits clear.
lessons.canDo: Compare two editorial positions and distinguish visit counts from unique visitors.

grammar.title: Acknowledge a point; keep the qualification
grammar.formation: Plain verb/i-adjective + とはいえ; noun/na-adjective (だ) + とはいえ. It can also begin a sentence referring to the previous statement.
grammar.explanation: Accept a fact or description, then add a judgement or outcome that the first part alone would not lead you to expect. The qualification matters to the conclusion. It does not necessarily mean the first fact was false.
grammar.example: 夜の利用時間が増えるとはいえ、職員の休憩も確保しなければならない。
grammar.translation: Even though evening access will increase, staff breaks must also be secured.

examples.ja: {夜|よる}の{利用時間|りようじかん}が{増|ふ}えるとはいえ、{職員|しょくいん}の{休憩|きゅうけい}も{確保|かくほ}しなければならない。
examples.en: Even though evening access will increase, staff breaks must also be secured.

examples.ja: {予算|よさん}は{少|すこ}ない。とはいえ、{三週間|さんしゅうかん}の{試行|しこう}は{可能|かのう}だ。
examples.en: The budget is small. Still, a three-week trial is possible.

examples.ja: {便利|べんり}だとはいえ、{予約|よやく}だけでは{借|か}りられない{本|ほん}もある。
examples.en: Even though it is convenient, some books cannot be borrowed through a reservation alone.

grammar.mistake: Do not translate every concession as a rejection of the acknowledged fact. Several connectors overlap; follow the whole argument.

grammar.title: A formal concession does not erase the limit
grammar.formation: Plain statement + といえども. A noun can directly precede it; noun/na-adjective predicates can include だ/である in a fuller clause.
grammar.explanation: A marked formal concession can take a noteworthy or extreme case and deny the expected consequence. Recognition in editorials and quoted statements is the focus; friends normally use plainer wording outside quotation.
grammar.example: 館長といえども、一人で開館時間を決められるわけではない。
grammar.translation: Even the library director cannot decide opening hours alone.

examples.ja: {館長|かんちょう}といえども、{一人|ひとり}で{開館時間|かいかんじかん}を{決|き}められるわけではない。
examples.en: Even the library director cannot decide opening hours alone.

examples.ja: たとえ{短|みじか}い{試行|しこう}といえども、{職員|しょくいん}の{勤務時間|きんむじかん}を{確認|かくにん}する{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.en: Even a short trial requires checking staff working hours.

examples.ja: {予算|よさん}が{増|ふ}えたといえども、{使|つか}い{道|みち}が{全|すべ}て{決|き}まったわけではない。
examples.en: Even though the budget increased, not all of its uses have been decided.

grammar.mistake: This form is not a causal because. Do not make とはいえ and といえども rivals in a gap when both fit; assess register or meaning with context.

grammar.title: A stated claim meets a practical qualification
grammar.formation: Plain statement + とはいうものの; noun/na-adjective predicates may include だ. Sentence-initial use can refer back to a stated claim.
grammar.explanation: Acknowledge something said, proposed or commonly described, then qualify how it works in practice. Here the notice and an actual proposal supply that claim. This can overlap with とはいえ; no absolute quoted-versus-unquoted ban is taught.
grammar.example: 夜間利用を認めるとはいうものの、今は金曜日だけの試行だ。
grammar.translation: Although evening use is being allowed, for now the trial is only on Fridays.

examples.ja: {夜間|やかん}{利用|りよう}を{認|みと}めるとはいうものの、{今|いま}は{金曜日|きんようび}だけの{試行|しこう}だ。
examples.en: Although evening use is being allowed, for now the trial is only on Fridays.

examples.ja: {延長|えんちょう}は{好評|こうひょう}だとはいうものの、{毎晩|まいばん}{続|つづ}ける{人件費|じんけんひ}はまだ{計算|けいさん}していない。
examples.en: Although the extension is well received, we haven't calculated the personnel cost of continuing every evening.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{書架|しょか}を{入|い}れるという{案|あん}がある。とはいうものの、{置|お}く{場所|ばしょ}はまだ{決|き}まっていない。
examples.en: There's a proposal to add a new book stack. That said, its location hasn't been decided yet.

grammar.mistake: Do not infer permanent approval from a generally worded claim; retain its actual timing and conditions. The final clause is not automatically total opposition.

grammar.title: An unattained extent, then a lesser one
grammar.formation: Verb negative form + までも; noun/na-adjective + ではないまでも is also recognised.
grammar.explanation: A greater or extreme extent is not asserted/reached, but a lesser extent remains: not every evening, but selected evenings; not eliminating a problem, but reducing it. Both desirable and undesirable scales occur. This is not doing nothing, and it differs from までもない (no need).
grammar.example: 毎晩開けられないまでも、週に一度は利用できるようにしたい。
grammar.translation: Even if we can't open every evening, we'd like to make it available once a week.

examples.ja: {毎晩|まいばん}{開|あ}けられないまでも、{週|しゅう}に{一度|いちど}は{利用|りよう}できるようにしたい。
examples.en: Even if we can't open every evening, we'd like to make it available once a week.

examples.ja: {待|ま}ち{時間|じかん}をなくせないまでも、{短|みじか}くする{工夫|くふう}はできる。
examples.en: Even if we can't eliminate the wait, we can find ways to shorten it.

examples.ja: {十分|じゅうぶん}な{予算|よさん}ではないまでも、{今月|こんげつ}の{試行|しこう}に{必要|ひつよう}な{額|がく}はある。
examples.en: Even if the budget isn't ample, we have the amount needed for this month's trial.

grammar.mistake: Keep the scale meaningful. In 開けられないまでも, ない belongs to the verb negative; it does not mean there is no need to open.

dialogues.title: Three Fridays, not every evening
dialogues.context: Ren and Hana compare a library notice with an editorial before the trial starts.

grammar: an acknowledged point versus the final recommendation
the scope and conditions of a stated claim
an unattained greater extent and a lesser proposal
watch.prompt: Optionally mark a conceded point and its qualification in material you supply. Identify the final recommendation from the whole passage. If listening, first identify the decision without a transcript, then check the wording.

recycling.reason: Only 原稿 naturally returns in the actual draft discussion. Do not force unrelated recent vocabulary into an everyday library exchange. Supplementary editorial headwords remain in the word list.

exercises.prompt: What has been decided when Ren and Hana read the notice?
options: A three-week Friday trial until eight
Permanent eight-o’clock closing every evening
A trial of closing at six instead of eight
exercises.explain: Ren says 三週間だけ. The trial is decided; hours after it remain undecided.

exercises.prompt: Does the article reject the entire extension because it mentions staff workload?
options: Yes; its conclusion cancels the trial
No; it recommends deciding after the three-week trial
Yes; it says nobody should use the library
exercises.explain: The stated conclusion is to try it and then decide. A concession is not total rejection.

exercises.prompt: What does the quoted 館長といえども line say?
options: The director alone already set permanent hours
Because they are the director, no consultation is needed
Even the director cannot decide alone
exercises.explain: The concession denies the expected unilateral power; it does not supply a causal justification.

exercises.prompt: Complete this acknowledged fact followed by a qualification, using the target とはいえ frame.
exercises.line: {便利|べんり}になる＿＿、{職員|しょくいん}の{負担|ふたん}も{考|かんが}えるべきだ。
options: とはいえ
とはいえるから
とはいえたので
exercises.explain: とはいえ introduces the qualification. The alternatives turn it into causal wording.

exercises.prompt: Choose the specifically requested といえども editorial register for: even the director cannot decide alone.
options: {館長|かんちょう}だから、{一人|ひとり}で{決|き}めていい。
{館長|かんちょう}といえども、{一人|ひとり}では{決|き}められない。
{館長|かんちょう}が{一人|ひとり}で{決|き}めた。
exercises.explain: The prompt requests the marked editorial concession. The other meanings give permission or assert a completed decision; this is not a contest between interchangeable concessive forms.

exercises.prompt: The discussion keeps a three-week trial possible despite a limited budget. Choose a response that preserves both facts.
options: うん、もう{試行|しこう}は{中止|ちゅうし}になったよ。
{予算|よさん}は{十分|じゅうぶん}だから、{毎晩|まいばん}{開|あ}けるよ。
{予算|よさん}は{少|すく}ない。とはいえ、{三週間|さんしゅうかん}の{試行|しこう}は{可能|かのう}だよ。
exercises.explain: The correct reply retains the limited budget and the possible trial. Neither cancellation nor ample funds/daily opening is the stated situation.
exercises.line: {予算|よさん}が{少|すく}ないから、{試行|しこう}もできないの？
exercises.meaning: Is the trial impossible too because the budget is small?

exercises.prompt: Ren has overread the actual notice. Choose Hana’s correction.
options: そうじゃないよ。{今|いま}は{金曜日|きんようび}だけの{試行|しこう}だよ。
そうだよ。{毎晩|まいばん}の{延長|えんちょう}が{正式|せいしき}に{決|き}まったよ。
いや、{図書館|としょかん}は{来月|らいげつ}から{全|すべ}て{閉|し}まるよ。
exercises.explain: The correction keeps the Friday-only trial. The notice neither approves permanent daily opening nor closes the library altogether.
exercises.line: {夜間|やかん}{利用|りよう}が{認|みと}められたなら、{毎晩|まいばん}{使|つか}えるんだね。
exercises.meaning: If evening access has been approved, we can use it every evening, then.

exercises.prompt: Which three things will they consider after the trial?
options: Book covers, rainy days, and the director’s favourite novel
User numbers, personnel costs, and whether staff took breaks
Only a high user count; no other conditions
exercises.explain: Hana names the count, 人件費 and staff breaks. A high count alone does not decide daily opening.

exercises.prompt: Use the taught とはいうものの construction to qualify the announced evening access.
exercises.line: {夜間|やかん}{利用|りよう}を{認|みと}める＿＿、{今|いま}は{金曜日|きんようび}だけの{試行|しこう}だ。
options: とはいったので
といえば必ず
とはいうものの
exercises.explain: The stated claim is qualified by the Friday-only trial. Causal or invariably wording does not express this relation.

exercises.prompt: What is the editorial’s final recommendation?
options: Support starting the trial, then examine three weeks of records and both groups before choosing a next plan
Commit to permanent nightly hours before observing the trial
Cancel all evening access because personnel costs exist
exercises.explain: The last paragraph supports the trial with a reservation about an immediate permanent commitment.

exercises.prompt: Why does the editorial request information beyond the user count?
options: All counts have been declared useless
A low count can still matter greatly to a user, and a high count can conceal concentrated staff workload
The director has banned speaking to staff
exercises.explain: The fifth paragraph supplies both cases and combines numbers with users’ reasons and staff conditions.

exercises.prompt: Order the blocks: although evening use is being allowed, the trial is only on Fridays for now.
exercises.explain: The acknowledged announcement precedes its actual restricted scope.
tiles: {夜間|やかん}{利用|りよう}を{認|みと}める
{今|いま}は{金曜日|きんようび}だけの
exercises.meaning: Although evening use is being allowed, the trial is only on Fridays for now.

exercises.prompt: Why should the notice clearly show the Friday-only condition?
options: So the library can secretly reject all visitors
Because it has already become permanent daily access
So visitors are not disappointed at the entrance and ending time can be kept
exercises.explain: The fourth paragraph explains realistic expectations and the closing boundary, not universal refusal.

exercises.prompt: What does Ren say about adding twenty-six and thirty-four?
options: They may include the same people, so sixty distinct people is not established
Exactly sixty different people are confirmed
No one came to either session
exercises.explain: Two session counts do not establish a unique-person count. Ren does not deny that visitors came.

exercises.prompt: Is continuing Fridays already confirmed after two sessions?
options: Yes; every evening is permanently approved
No; it is a proposal awaiting the final session and staff input
Yes; the trial has ended after only two sessions
exercises.explain: Hana says まだ提案 and identifies what still needs to happen.

exercises.prompt: What does 毎晩開けられないまでも、週に一度は利用できるようにしたい express?
options: There is no need to open at all
Once a week has already been permanently approved
Even if nightly opening is not possible, a once-weekly option is desired
exercises.explain: The unattained greater frequency leaves a desired lesser extent. It is a wish, not proof of approval.

exercises.prompt: Use the negative form of 開けられる before までも in the target frame.
exercises.line: {毎晩|まいばん}＿＿までも、{週|しゅう}に{一度|いちど}は{利用|りよう}できるようにしたい。
options: {開|あ}けられない
{開|あ}けられて
{開|あ}けられます
exercises.explain: ないまでも requires the negative verb form here. The te/polite forms are not this attachment.

exercises.prompt: What staff information has the writer actually obtained?
options: Every staff member has agreed
One staff member said closing preparations were busy; other staff have not yet been heard
The director has promised unlimited personnel spending
exercises.explain: The fourth paragraph explicitly limits the interview to one staff member and defers other views.

exercises.prompt: Which conclusion matches the response?
options: Decide permanent nightly opening immediately
Accept the trial but ignore its result
Consider continuing Fridays after the final trial record and staff costs/workload are examined
exercises.explain: The final paragraph retains support and conditions; it neither commits to daily opening nor discards the trial.

exercises.prompt: What do both editorials support, despite being written at different times?
options: Using the trial and both users’ and staff information before deciding ongoing hours
Treating two sessions as enough to approve nightly opening
Ignoring personnel costs because convenience alone settles the decision
exercises.explain: The first supports starting and reviewing three weeks; the second, after two sessions, still waits for the final session and staff input.
